data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.spec_note: mass/power fields are taken from the first sentence in the NASA description that states a mass in kg or a power in W; they may describe a sub-unit or a mode. Read the sentence.
record.name: Engineering Experiments
record.description: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter will carry three instruments designated as engineering experiments. These instruments, designed to assist in spacecraft navigation and communications, will be operated and assessed for use on future missions. Electra UHF Communications and Navigation Package Electra allows the spacecraft to act as a communications relay between the Earth and landed crafts on Mars that may not have sufficient radio power to communicate directly with Earth by themselves. Optical Navigation Camera This camera is being tested for improved navigation capability for future missions. If it performs well, similar cameras placed on orbiters of the future would be able to serve as high-precision interplanetary "eyes" to guide incoming spacecraft as they near Mars. Ka-band Telecommunications Experiment Package Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter will test the use of a radio frequency called Ka-band to demonstrate the potential for greater performance in communications using significantly less power.
record.text_extraction_note: numeric_mentions_in_text are regex matches of 'number unit' in the catalog prose, with context; they are not structured specifications.
